PASS applies only to the scoped A–G extension. General S11 remains open. I independently checked the supplied current article, both historical divisor-removal and blowup arguments, the new private F–G proof, the complete ruled-family article, and reconstruction notes n1–n7. Historical verdicts, candidate flags, hashes, read records and computational artifacts were not proof premises. The historical drafts’ additional zero-Lelong assumption is not inherited by the current B.

A. The regularization application is valid. T=dd^c q' is closed and almost positive, with smooth closed representative 0, source potential ψ=q'/2, and continuous real lower bound γ=εh−B. The lower bound need not be closed. Choose the tangent metric induced by h. Compactness bounds its Griffiths curvature below by −Ch⊗Id, so the stronger sufficient hypothesis holds with u=Ch. Zero Lelong numbers make every positive level set E_s(T) empty. The continuous decreasing λ_k converge uniformly to zero by Dini’s theorem; ε_k also tends to zero. Consequently the entire curvature loss is at most εh/2 for a sufficiently large k. The global smooth function f=2ψ_(s,k) satisfies the claimed inequality. This uses the established attenuation and smoothing mechanism, with smoothing applied to continuous intermediate potentials. It asserts no ordinary equivalence between f and q'. The supplied Section 2 proof supports this application; the general Section 5 route is unnecessary. The author-hosted PDF timed out during retrieval, but the matching author-uploaded [primary paper](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/247379399_Regularization_of_Closed_Positive_Currents_and_Intersection_Theory) was accessible.

E. The automatic vanishing proof establishes the previously missing antecedent for B. For n≥2, Gauduchon’s Theorem 2 supplies a smooth positive γ with dd^c γ^(n−1)=0. Its complete printed proof uses the adjoint elliptic kernel and maximum principle; the separate even-Betti theorem is irrelevant. For n=1, γ^0=1 suffices without that theorem. Each actual same-type representative gives the positive global current T_δ=dd^c q_δ+δh and the exact identity ∫T_δ∧γ^(n−1)=δ∫h∧γ^(n−1). Closedness of T_δ is unnecessary for this distributional Stokes pairing.

On finitely many fixed nested coordinate domains, choose fixed quadratics ρ_a with dd^cρ_a≥h. Then p_(δ,a)=q_δ+δρ_a is genuine psh, and its Hessian is closed and positive. Since dd^c p_(δ,a)=T_δ+δ(dd^cρ_a−h), metric comparison and the finite smooth correction bound its local Euclidean trace by C_aδ. The charts have compact closures and finite volume; every point in the smaller chart has a ball of one fixed positive radius inside the larger chart. The trace theorem is applied with bidimension p=n−1, including p=0 when n=1. It bounds every point Lelong number by Cδ. Smooth additions and mutual bounded order preserve the logarithmic growth coefficient, so the bound transfers to q. Letting δ tend to zero proves vanishing everywhere. The source Hessian operator is twice the task operator; this only changes fixed positive constants, not vanishing. No approximation changing the ordinary type establishes or substitutes for the hypothesis.

F. Canonical pullback is valid on every stated modification. After a local smooth correction, it is the holomorphic pullback of a genuine psh function. Every source open set meets the locus where the modification is biholomorphic, so this pullback is not identically minus infinity there and is locally integrable. Both ordinary inequalities pull back pointwise, including poles. Compactness gives π*h≤Ch'. The sharp curvature inequality also survives: locally correct q_δ by δρ to obtain a positive pullback Hessian; on the biholomorphic complement retain the sharper bound −δπ*h, and across the exceptional analytic set retain it by restricting coefficient measures, since the smooth correction has no mass there. Thus dd^cπ*q_δ≥−Cδh'. For any requested loss η, choose δ≤η/C. These are actual representatives in [π*q]. Applying E upstairs proves zero point Lelong numbers. This argument requires neither factorization nor a pullback theorem for arbitrary zero-Lelong functions.

B. Divisor removal retains the exact nonclosed lower bound. Omit zero coefficients and let A be the remaining support. Off A, subtract the logarithmic potential. In a local trivialization, q'+ρ−σ=v+ρ−Σa_j log|g_j|² is psh and locally bounded above by the ordinary comparison with q. Canonical pluripolar removability produces its genuine extension. Off A its Hessian has the sharper smooth lower bound dd^cρ−θ+εh. On A the extended positive Hessian has a positive matrix of coefficient measures, whereas that smooth bound has zero measure restriction. Hence B+dd^c q'≥εh globally, without assuming B closed. Adding a common local smooth correction and recovering canonical psh values by ball averages extends both inequalities q'≤q+C and q≤q'+C across A, including poles. Almost-everywhere equality also gives v=ell_Δ+q' canonically. E and bounded difference supply zero Lelong numbers for q'; A then supplies the required smooth gauge.

Conversely, a smooth positive gauge has a uniform margin εh on compact M. Choose an actual q_δ~q with δ<ε/2 and put v=ell_Δ+q_δ+f. Poincaré–Lelong gives θ+dd^c v=[Δ]+B+dd^c f+dd^c q_δ≥εh/2. This sum is genuine and mutually equivalent to ell_Δ+q, including its poles. The zero-divisor case uses the identically zero logarithmic term. No singular potential is restricted to a divisor. If dimension zero is allowed in A or B, the form inequalities are vacuous and the conclusions are immediate.

C. The explicit representatives work at every finite stage. The piecewise χ_L matches both value and derivative at −L, is convex and increasing, and satisfies 0≤χ'_L≤η_L→0. Its unchanged singular tail differs from χ by a finite constant, while the remaining argument interval is compact. Thus U_L~U, with the same genuine minus-infinity values, and dd^cU_L≥−η_Lw_1. The punctured inequality extends canonically across D. Its genuine pullbacks remain in [π*U] and have curvature at least −Cη_Lh'.

The direct Lelong check covers all infinitely near points. A local equation g of the total transform is a nonzero holomorphic germ. At any zero it has finite order N and a direction ξ with nonzero leading homogeneous term. Along tξ, log|g|²=2N log|t|+O(1), so π*U is bounded below by −C|log|t||^α−C. Its spherical supremum has the same lower bound. After a smooth psh correction, division by the negative logarithm bounds the nonnegative growth coefficient above by a quantity tending to zero. Away from the total transform the function is smooth. This establishes the specified family’s conclusion without a universal zero-Lelong pullback assumption.

D. Apply B with divisor bπ*D, residual π*U and residual background π*β. The last exceptional curve is smooth and contracted by the composite map. A hypothetical smooth positive gauge restricts there to dd^c(f|E)>0, since π*β|E=0. Curve Stokes gives a contradiction. Only the smooth f is restricted, so centers in the original poles or earlier exceptional divisors cause no difficulty.

The recursive one-sided witness is also actual. The exceptional bundle O(E)|E=O(−1) permits a smooth metric whose curvature B_E is negative on the exceptional tangent; its metric extends smoothly to O(E). In finitely many bounded blowup charts, the pullback metric matrix P has P_xx≥c_0, mixed coefficient O(|x|), and Schur complement at least c_1|x|². The Schur complement after adding −tB_E is bounded below by c_1|x|²+tb_0−C(t|x|+t|x|²+t²). First fix a sufficiently small exceptional neighborhood, then choose t sufficiently small. The horizontal coefficient stays positive and the error terms consume less than half the vertical margin. On the compact complement, a sufficiently small perturbation preserves positivity. Hence π*h_j−tB_E is an actual smooth positive form with a uniform Hermitian lower bound.

Starting with bG_p+U_L, whose downstairs strictness follows from η_L<c−b and min a>0, the recursive potential π*v_j+δ_jt_j ell_E therefore remains strict. Pullbacks and sums are genuine even over pole centers. Each logarithm is globally bounded above, so induction preserves v'≤π*r+C. The obstruction proves that the resulting witness has a different ordinary type. Separately, the task-granted full competitor bijection and actual non-pluripolar pushforward law apply to every competitor in [π*r]. They preserve both optimized masses, yielding exactly 2(c−b)min a and 2(c−b)max a. The witness’s added exceptional poles are not inserted into that optimization. These mass laws are granted input, not a newly proved universal criterion.

G. Zero-Lelong integrability is reconstructed from the imported Bergman theorem. On a bounded pseudoconvex coordinate ball, correct q to a psh φ. For fixed m>0, the weighted Hilbert unit ball has uniformly bounded local first derivatives: the local upper bound on φ controls its unweighted L² norm, and mean-value and Cauchy estimates then apply on nested compact neighborhoods. If every weighted holomorphic function vanished at x, this would give |g(z)|≤C|z−x| uniformly on that unit ball. The evaluation-norm formula would imply φ_m(z)≤m^(−1)log|z−x|+C, hence ν(φ_m,x)≥1/m. This contradicts ν(φ_m,x)≤ν(φ,x)=0. An actual weighted function is therefore nonzero at x and bounded away from zero after shrinking. Its finite weighted norm proves e^(−2mφ) locally integrable. Taking 2m=s and undoing the bounded smooth correction proves the assertion for every s>0.

For ideal neutrality, the local upper bound on q gives I(t(v+q))⊂I(tv). If g∈I(tv), correct v locally to psh and apply strong openness with source parameter c=t/2. It supplies p>1 for which |g|²e^(−ptv) is integrable on a smaller neighborhood. Let p'=p/(p−1). The preceding integrability result and local boundedness of g make |g|²e^(−p'tq) integrable. Hölder applies to the exact factorization (|g|²e^(−ptv))^(1/p)(|g|²e^(−p'tq))^(1/p')=|g|²e^(−t(v+q)). Both exponents are positive and conjugate; the holomorphic factor retains precisely power 2. Bounded smooth corrections preserve each assertion. This proves equality at every stalk and every real t>0, for every v. Taking v=ell_Δ covers arbitrary effective real divisors.

For the SNC trace, polar integration gives I(t ell_Δ)=O_M(−Σ floor(ta_j)D_j). A transverse order k is allowed precisely when k+1>ta_j. At an integer ta_j=N, order N−1 leaves exponent −2 and diverges; order N succeeds. Factoring the allowed powers leaves all remaining exponents strictly above −2, proving sufficiency; a nonzero leading tangential coefficient proves necessity. Only positive-coefficient components enter restricted equations and orders. Connectedness and the noncontainment hypothesis make each relevant local equation on Y a nonzero germ. Its pullback under every stated modification remains nonzero and has a finite nonnegative order N_(j,E). The exact restricted ambient ideal order is Σ_(a_j>0) floor(ta_j)N_(j,E); division by t gives the displayed finite trace. Generic ambient Lelong number along Y is zero away from the positive divisor components. None of this uses q|Y, which may be identically minus infinity, or infers envelope exactness from lower inequalities.

The complete supporting ruled-family proofs also check out independently. Both χ_L and the alternative shifted Green power give actual same-type small-curvature tails and strict downstairs representatives throughout b<c. Canonical removal and fiber averaging exclude b≥c. For every rough residual q~U, use the closed dominating K=C(w_1+w_2). The currents K+dd^c q and the separated reference are positive, closed, cohomologous, and locally bounded outside the closed pluripolar divisor D. The [BEGZ comparison](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~guedj/fichierspdf/BEGZ10.pdf) therefore applies in degrees one and two, in both ordinary orders. Degree one removes the positive polar defect by its zero K-trace; degree two gives full auxiliary closed mass. The finite smooth-background expansion yields M(v)=∫β²+2∫q dd^cβ=2∫aσ, with σ a positive curve measure of mass c−b. Both extremizing constructions give actual same-type competitors concentrating σ at either extremum, including p. Sphere Poisson statements can be realized directly by smooth Green-kernel convolution, so no additional existence theorem is needed.

The supporting transverse ideal calculation has the correct floor endpoints. The separated first-moment tail is 2Cα(1−α)T^(2α−2)dT, giving finiteness exactly for α<1/2 and the stated logarithmic divergence at equality. Canonical descent, locality and absence of non-pluripolar mass on analytic sets establish the full pullback bijection and pushforward identity. Both outside-pole blowup witnesses are valid, with the bounded restriction hypothesis established for their obstruction. Both all-test Gauduchon-volume proofs cover mixed and fiber-dependent tests; the attaining test, signed derivative and integrated subtraction formula are correct. The numerical example, infinite-moment assertion and distinction between identical ideal traces and different ordinary types follow analytically. [BGL’s definitions and divisorial/modification credit](https://d-nb.info/1374372846/34) are confirmed; they are not substituted for the explicit calculations.

The support graph is acyclic. For the current extension: A uses regularization; E uses the global trace and local Lelong foundations; F uses E and canonical pullback; B uses E, divisor removal and A; C uses its explicit representatives and growth calculation; D uses B, C, the recursive metric argument and the separately granted mass laws; G uses Bergman approximation, openness, E where required, and the SNC integral calculation. The supplied historical graph is n1; n2←n1; n3←n1; n4←n1,n2,n3; n5←n1,n2,n3; n6←n2; n7←n1,…,n6. All supplied parent proofs were checked; redundant edges are harmless. The unrelated companion coefficient and envelope assertions are outside this graph.

Harmless corrections must be explicit. Gauduchon’s conformal uniqueness statement is used only for n≥2; the manuscript’s phrase “every complex dimension” should be narrowed accordingly, since n=1 is handled separately. The convolution identity in support note n1 is exact when its smooth correction is quadratic; for a general smooth correction it needs the additional term (dd^c k)*ρ_ε−dd^c k, which also tends uniformly to zero. In the Bergman source, uniform kernel convergence is needed only on compact subsets. In Section 2, “uniformly bounded” must mean bounded above, almost-everywhere and sliced convergence require a subsequence, and the displayed 1 in F_(j,l) must be f_l. The actual scaling application for Corollary 2.3 already has the required pointwise and sliced convergence. The 1992 smoothing lemma is used only for continuous intermediates, not as its overbroad printed pole-bearing formulation. These corrections leave the proofs and conclusions intact; no substantial repair is needed. Ohsawa–Takegoshi, Kiselman, Richberg and analytic-division foundations retain their stated imported status and credit.

passages.statement: Demailly’s 1992 Main Theorem 1.1, with its Section 2 stronger curvature hypothesis, states: on a compact Hermitian manifold (M,h), let T=α+(i/π)∂bar∂ψ be a closed almost positive real (1,1)-current, with α smooth closed real and ψ genuine quasi-psh, and let γ be any continuous real (1,1)-form satisfying T≥γ. If a selected smooth tangent metric has Griffiths curvature c(TM)+u⊗Id≥0 for a smooth semipositive form u, then for every s>0 there are global potentials ψ_(s,k), smooth on M\{ν(T,·)≥s}, satisfying α+(i/π)∂bar∂ψ_(s,k)≥γ−min(λ_k,s)u−ε_kh, where λ_k are continuous and decrease pointwise to ν(T,·), and ε_k>0 decreases to zero. γ need not be closed.

passages.statement: For 1≤p≤n, non-pluripolar products of closed positive (1,1)-currents on a compact Kähler n-manifold are well defined, positive, closed and of finite mass, and put no mass on pluripolar sets. They are local in the plurifine topology. For potentials locally bounded outside a closed locally complete pluripolar set, the product is the trivial extension of the bounded Bedford–Taylor product from its complement. Locally, ⟨dd^cφ⟩=1_{φ>−∞}dd^cφ. These are BEGZ §1.2, Proposition 1.6 and Theorem 1.8.

For a genuine psh function φ on a coordinate domain, with the source convention dd^c_src=(i/π)∂bar∂, ν(dd^c_srcφ,x)=lim_(r→0) sup_(|z−x|=r)φ(z)/log r. Consequently smooth additions and mutual bounded difference preserve this growth coefficient; replacing dd^c_src by (i/(2π))∂bar∂ scales the current Lelong number by 1/2.

Demailly’s arXiv:1401.5432v2 Theorem 1.2 states: for a genuine psh φ on a bounded pseudoconvex domain Ω⊂C^n and every real m>0, let H_Ω(mφ) consist of holomorphic functions with finite integral ∫_Ω|g|²e^(−2mφ)dV. For an orthonormal basis (g_(m,l)), the potential φ_m=(1/(2m))logΣ_l|g_(m,l)|² is psh; its kernel equals sup_(||g||≤1)|g(z)|², and ν(φ,x)−n/m≤ν(φ_m,x)≤ν(φ,x) at every x∈Ω.

Guan–Zhou strong openness, as stated in Demailly’s arXiv:1401.5432v2 Corollary 2.3 with the supplied Hiep proof, states: if φ is genuine psh near x, g is holomorphic near x, c>0, and |g|²e^(−2cφ) is locally integrable near x, then there exists c'>c for which |g|²e^(−2c'φ) is integrable on a possibly smaller neighborhood of x.

For 1≤p≤n, non-pluripolar products of closed positive (1,1)-currents on a compact Kähler n-manifold are well defined, positive, closed and of finite mass, and put no mass on pluripolar sets. They are local in the plurifine topology. For potentials locally bounded outside a closed locally complete pluripolar set, the product is the trivial extension of the bounded Bedford–Taylor product from its complement. Locally, ⟨dd^cφ⟩=1_{φ>−∞}dd^cφ. These are BEGZ §1.2, Proposition 1.6 and Theorem 1.8.

BEGZ Theorem 1.16 states: on a compact Kähler n-manifold, for 1≤p≤n, let T_j and T'_j be cohomologous closed positive (1,1)-currents with small unbounded locus, meaning local boundedness of potentials outside a closed locally complete pluripolar set. If every T_j is less singular than T'_j in ordinary bounded order, then {⟨T_1∧…∧T_p⟩}−{⟨T'_1∧…∧T'_p⟩} is represented by a closed positive (p,p)-current.
